A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central theory, experimental systems and identifiable appendices. Full text comparison and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, table and supplementary material without unresolved extraction gaps.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix J report original simulations of mean-field RNNs, two-well Langevin dynamics, and nine chaotic systems with observers, including convergence and runtime measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix K retain original simulation results for RNNs, Langevin dynamics and chaotic observers, including convergence measurements, runtime comparisons and analyses across random seeds.

M1.justification: The DEER/Gauss-Newton updates, parallel-scan procedure, quasi-DEER diagonal approximation and contractive weight parameterization in Appendix I are retained. New Appendix J interprets existing DEER iterations as linear dynamical system layers without changing their computation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mean-field RNN family, two-well Langevin system, and nine dysts chaotic flows with corresponding observers. Newly discussed language models and sequence-model architectures do not introduce additional evaluations performed by this work.

E2.justification: The optimizer comparison in v2 Figure 6 and v3 Figure 7 retains DEER, quasi-DEER and gradient descent for convergence, with sequential evaluation additionally included for runtime. Newly cited methods such as ParaSolver and ParaRNN do not enter these reported comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 Appendix K states that experiments report continuous-time LLE estimates; v3 Appendix L instead specifies discrete-time LLEs generally, with Table 1 explicitly retaining continuous-time estimates. This changes the stated metric normalization. The PDFs do not establish that simulations were rerun or that newly disclosed integration steps changed.

E4.justification: The sensitivity/calibration analysis relating RNN variance parameter g to LLE is revised: v2 Figure 4 becomes v3 Figure 5, showing a near-zero plateau instead of the earlier smooth rise. The numerical-divergence case study, alternative-optimizer analysis and supplementary Langevin and observer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 20-seed median/min-max summaries, five-seed optimizer study with five timing runs per seed, and averaging over three initial vectors for LLE estimation. The revised calibration curve retains the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 3's two-well LLE changes from -1.45 to -0.0145, consistent with the revised normalization rather than a performance gain. Figure 2's experimental heatmap and the g-to-LLE curve in v2 Figure 4/v3 Figure 5 are revised. Table 1 and the optimizer-runtime comparison retain their reported results.

T1.justification: Appendix C replaces the zero-LLE upper bound sqrt(mu) <= 1/b with sqrt(mu) <= sqrt(2D/(T+1))/b and supplies a new Frobenius-norm derivation. This establishes conditioning deterioration with sequence length in the neutral case. The main nonzero-LLE bounds and convergence theorems remain; the continuous-time variational equation is also corrected.

C1.justification: The central predictability, conditioning and O((log T)^2) parallelization claims remain. The abstract replaces its explicit exponential-degradation statement with less specific degradation wording. Section 6 adds a third implication: interpreting a stable nonlinear SSM as O(log T) nonlinearly coupled linear dynamical system layers.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds the semiseparable-matrix/Mamba2 connection and possible implications for hardware acceleration. Section 6 and new Appendix J develop the layer-stack interpretation, while v3 also attributes ParaRNN's rapid convergence to contractivity. Existing memory, numerical-precision and initialization limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies T=9999 for the RNN LLE calibration, a Langevin step size of 0.01, and Euler step size 0.01 for every Table 1 system. These are additional disclosures, not demonstrated changes to the underlying simulations. FP64, hardware, optimizer settings and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion and citations concerning local Gauss-Newton convergence, additional parallel diffusion solvers, ParaRNN and Mamba2/state-space duality, while removing Nesterov's 2018 Lectures reference. These expand the surrounding research context while retaining the central novelty positioning around LLE-controlled merit-function conditioning.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, Section 6 is renamed Discussion and reorganized around three implications, and a new interpretive Appendix J precedes the experimental appendix, now K. Terminology and acknowledgments receive smaller edits. Most existing theoretical and experimental exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figure 4 illustrating the nonlinear-SSM/linear-layer equivalence, revises Figure 2's axes and presentation, and replots the calibration figure with an expanded caption. Table 1's caption gains the Euler step size. Existing appendix figures are renumbered and reflowed; most displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: Appendix C's stronger zero-LLE bound and the newly disclosed step sizes provide limited gains in analytical completeness and reproducibility. Figure 3's renormalized exponent better aligns that result with the discrete-time theory. These gains are tempered by Figure 8 retaining its earlier LLE scale and new Appendix J leaving Section 4's T-independent overshoot qualification implicit in its logarithmic-depth interpretation.
